Alrighty. Frizz often indicates that your hair texture is actually more wavy or curly than you'd think. Mine was always super frizzy and I hated it. My mom gave me a copy of this and I decided to give it a try. It took a month for my hair to adapt but I discovered that my hair is wavy/curly, not just a sad frizzy mess. I would highly recommend you find yourself a copy of this and give it a read. I have since refined my haircare routine and it's been pretty awesome for my hair.

Basically, you want to use a sulfate-free shampoo and only shampoo your scalp; comb your hair in the shower between shampooing and conditioning; and use a technique called "squish to condish" for your conditioner. You can google that one but the gist of it is that you flip your hair upside down in the shower (so you're bent over dangling your head with your hair hanging down) and then scrunch the conditioner into your hair for a few minutes. After a couple minutes of scrunching, you cup your hands under the shower and start scrunching handfuls of water into your hair until it feels like it's not slippery with conditioner anymore. What this does is push both conditioner and water up under the cuticle of the hair so it's nice and hydrated and happy.

So yeah. Give that a try and see if your texture doesn't change from frizzy to wavy. Often those of us with waves will find that the bits right around our faces will be curly and not just wavy. Give it a month. Your scalp and roots will probably look greasy as it gets used to the new shampoo; that's normal and it'll go away after a couple weeks or so. Once it settles you'll have a better idea of what your styling options are. Wavy hair is versatile! Currently I've got mine in a choppy chin-length bob, which I love because it's too short to put into a ponytail or bun and it looks really stylish just worn down and natural.

As far as "what do I do with my hair" goes, it depends on your personal fashion style. Mine is broad. I love bohemian; I love plaid and leather rocker chic looks; I love anything French inspired. So for me, a style that's wash and go, but has that loose, relaxed, messy natural vibe is what I like. It goes with all of my style "personalities". If your style is 50s inspired, or you prefer tailored clothes in more classic shapes, you'll want to look for styles that are refined and feminine.

Late posting but my hair sounds similar to yours as far as the frizz goes. I have mine halfway down my back so with all of that weight (gravity) pulling on it my hair tends to not look nearly as wavy as it actually is. In the winter it's a nightmare, it's a messy, frizzy looking mess. I detest it. My hair seems to frizz worse when the weather is cold and the dry heat is circulating indoors.

I have a relative with really, really curly long hair whose hair is thick and hers is the opposite - it's the humidity that causes hers to frizz.

I would try to notice when your hair is at it's most frizzy and most unmanageable. If it tends to act up during the cold weather it's probably like my hair and isn't getting enough moisture during the winter and (at least in my case) applying more dry heat isn't going to help.

( I noticed that you said your hair isn't thin or thick. Mine is fine and it took me years to realize that because everyone would comment on how absolutely thick my hair is. It isn't. It's fine. I just have a TON of it. I don't know if that's what your hair is like too but I thought I would mention it because it literally took me years before I realized that yes, my hair is fine - there's just lots of it.)

To get rid of the winter time wavy, frizzy mess after I've had a shower (using sulfate free shampoo and conditioner and using a shower comb to make sure the conditioner pulls all the way through to the ends) and towel dried I use a round brush and a blow dryer to just pull it straight. Honestly I would avoid the blow dryer if I could but just trust me may hair just doesn't look good during cold weather when it dries naturally. I use sulfate free and paraben free products to add a bit of style and they are formulated to help protect from heat.

I try not to brush my hair after I've pulled all of the wave out while blow drying. It tends to make it frizz out even more and I do add Biosilk to my hair while it is damp before I blow dry. Sometimes I can't help it though and do have to run a brush through it but the Biosilk and trying not to brush it very much (to prevent breakage and frizz) is more due to my hair getting not just tangled but actually knotted.

I also try to towel dry as much as possible and blow dry as little as I can to try to avoid that dry heat.

I live in an extremely humid area and have found that in the summer with all of the humidity in the air my hair retains plenty of moisture and I can actually just let it dry naturally and I get a very loose looking wave to it minus the frizzy mess so I always try to give my hair a much needed break from the blow dryer during those months.

No matter the time of year hot rollers only frizz my hair out though. Curling irons - my hair is too fine to hold those curls plus that's a lot of heat damage (same reason that I will not use a flat iron). The only thing that I have ever found that helps in getting actual pretty curls in my hair are steam rollers (it's steam so no damage there and it really makes my hair smooth with zero frizz). It takes a while though because first I have to wash and dry and then roll so I normally don't bother unless it's a special event or I just feel like something different.

I will use Argon oil from about halfway down my hair all the way to the roots and I try to do this weekly to help repair and to retain moisture and I get my hair trimmed once a month. The major conflict of interest that I've found with adding more moisture to my hair via means of conditioner and/or oil is that I lose a lot of volume so I try to apply very little conditioner at the scalp and a ton on the ends. I also only apply the oil halfway down my hair to the ends.

Anyway, I know you were looking more for ways to style your hair but I saw all of the talk surrounding frizzy hair and it took me years before I realized that it was a winter time/lack of moisture thing going on for me. Hope that I could be of some help :)
